platform: Apple M1 Pro/macOS ARM64 Release; four platform workers for performance comparisons
candidate: working tree on 12.6-jsonparse-async; full Ninja rebuild
changes: Worker: predict direct bounded number conversion only after two consecutive non-Smi numeric results; reset on a Smi.
Sync NEON frontend: reuse the validated short-string prefix and character width; preserve the original dense-escape boundary.
Outline the NEON string probe so its fallback state stays out of recursive parsing loops.

protocol.order: AB BA BA AB for final paired cells
protocol.correctness: Each prototype must pass existing numeric/string/async regressions and a baseline edge differential before timing.
protocol.adoption: Only candidates with repeated target improvements proceed; reject reproducible control regressions. Final synchronous gate 3%, asynchronous gate 5%, requiring both aggregate and paired-median ratios.
protocol.scope: Mac ARM64 Release; 6 fixture families x 10/20/50 MB x 2 APIs; 6 four-job 20 MB async controls; 13 focused fixtures x 2 APIs.
protocol.host: Wait for observed compiler processes before each measurement. No task build, profiling or correctness run overlaps performance measurements.
protocol.timing: API wall time includes natural GC, worker scheduling, materialization and Promise completion. Explicit pre-round GC, input setup and full-result validation are outside the timed interval.
protocol.resources: CPU and peak RSS are whole-process values including startup, warmups, validation and explicit GC; these are not per-API allocation/CPU measurements.
protocol.micro_sizes: Focused fixtures are 1.4 to 6.54 million UTF-16 code units; they are workload-specific microbenchmarks, not tiny JSON latency claims.

pilot_disposition.worker-adaptive: Rejected: alternating Smi/double async microbenchmark regressed about 7%.
pilot_disposition.array-feedback: Rejected: Canada 20 MB sync regressed about 13%; double-pair microbenchmark regressed about 17%.
pilot_disposition.string-prefix: Superseded: escaped strings improved, but mixed_nested 20 MB sync exceeded the 3% guard in the pilot.
pilot_disposition.worker-streak: Positive prototype, consolidated duplicate bounded conversion into worker-streak-shared.
pilot_disposition.string-short-prefix: Rejected: Canada 20 MB sync regressed about 4.3%.
pilot_disposition.sync-empty-old: Rejected: CITM target improved but Canada 50 MB sync regressed about 4%. No allocation-policy change retained.
pilot_disposition.sync-empty-outline: Rejected: outlining did not fix the Canada control regression (about 6% at 50 MB).
pilot_disposition.string-outline: Advanced to full-build qualification with worker-streak-shared.
pilot_disposition.worker-streak-shared: Advanced to full-build qualification with string-outline.

evidence_boundaries: Final timings use the normal rebuilt production binary. Isolated object-relink prototypes are pilot evidence only.
All pilot results, including regressions, remain in the report and local raw directory.
Sampling profiles locate hot functions but do not provide exclusive API-phase timing.
No claim is made for Android/iOS/x64 runtime performance, tiny-input latency, application UI responsiveness or untested workloads.
